title: Marginalia Search, Money, C++, Rust, AI, Stuff
lede: The developer of Marginalia Search reports rising donations and API-key sales, a slow experimental port of the index from Java to C++, and why they will not let AI write it.

points: SerpApi sponsored the project with $10k, and other donations and key sales have grown monthly since summer; it is not yet self-sustaining.
Free API keys can take a week or two, because every request is handled by hand.
The index is CPU-bound, and Java's off-heap handling forces duplicate sorting and searching code; the buffer pool and part of the inverted index are now in C++.
The author chose C++ over Rust out of experience rather than language merit, and may still drop the port.
They decline AI translation because they could not maintain the result and will not depend on a subscription whose prices could rise.

points.text: Many backed the independence argument, treating a permanent AI subscription like renting from a landlord.
A reply argues the author overrates the difficulty, since you can ask a model to simplify and explain its code until it is maintainable.
Several suggested modern C# as an alternative with good native-memory support, one citing 30% to 300% speedups after porting.
Commenters split on whether the JVM is really the bottleneck, with one reply arguing Java is fast enough once the JIT warms up.
